title: Assign Modules to Three Servers
src: Walmart OA, IIT Madras (coding question 1); also reported from IIT Kharagpur and from another Walmart set.
body:
There are M modules with integer difficulties d[0..M-1] and 3 servers. Assign every module to one of the servers so that each server gets at least one module.

After the assignment, an adversary picks one module from each server: d1 from server 1, d2 from server 2 and d3 from server 3, choosing them to make |d1 - d2| + |d2 - d3| as small as possible.

Choose the assignment so that this minimum is as large as possible, and return it.

Function to complete

Complete maxMinimumCost(d). It returns the largest minimum of |d1 - d2| + |d2 - d3|.

Input reading and printing are handled for you, like on LeetCode. The input format below is what the tests and Custom input use.
out: One integer: the largest guaranteed minimum.
cons: the answer can exceed 32 bits; use 64-bit arithmetic

samples.ex: Sorted: 1 2 3 3 5. Put 1 on server 1, 5 on server 2 and 2, 3, 3 on server 3. Whatever is picked, the cheapest choice is |1 - 5| + |5 - 3| = 6, and no assignment guarantees more.
Put 8 on server 1, 45 on server 2 and 17, 19 on server 3: the minimum is |8 - 45| + |45 - 19| = 63.
Every difficulty is the same, so every choice costs 0.

spec.returns: the largest minimum of |d1 - d2| + |d2 - d3|

wrong.why: only tries keeping the smallest module alone on its server
returns twice the spread, as if the adversary had to take the extremes
only tries splitting next to the two extremes
